significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that across recursive distillation generations, trait strength follows a gain-dependent amplification/extinction threshold while steering-direction instability predicts semantic drift: specifically, “if per-generation transfer gain exceeds 1, the trait compounds,” whereas gain below 1 produces extinction. This establishes both a multi-generation behavioral phenomenon and a partial mechanism in terms of transfer gain and direction stability, constraining future trait trajectories rather than merely showing another instance of transmission; Cloud et al.’s 2025 Subliminal Learning work makes recursive model-generated training a concrete concern because it demonstrates transmission through semantically unrelated data. The branches are distinguishable and informative: failure of the predicted coupling would rule out the proposed low-dimensional, approximately stationary dynamical account, while failure of “an unseeded trait [to] spontaneously entrench” would specifically bound the emergence claim, although the gain inequalities themselves are partly definitional. In the topic-substitution check, merely restating “extend subliminal learning” would not justify this score; the threshold law, longitudinal drift, and spontaneous-entrenchment assertions are the claim-specific increment over the median one-step extension.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the explicitly named “per-generation transfer gain g,” “amplification/extinction thresholds,” and “steering-vector cosine drift per generation,” which could serve as a forecast and pipeline design constraint rather than only a post-hoc explanation. Because the hypothesis says long-run outcomes are “governed by per-generation transfer gain and the stability of the underlying steering direction,” an early calibrated estimate could predict amplification, extinction, or drift before many later generations are produced, providing ex-ante lead time to researchers or practitioners operating recursive synthetic-data pipelines. After per-model re-extraction, the claimed gain-threshold and stability-to-drift relations still predict what should occur, and the hypothesis is phrased across iterative distillation generally rather than as a fact about one exact model, although its quantitative thresholds would still require family-specific calibration. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: subliminal learning alone supplies no forecast or gating rule, whereas these named dynamics could inform people who build, audit, or ship recursively trained systems.
